_what: The operating point: the one server command line every measurement and every instruction has to agree with.
_why: It was spelled out in three places that disagreed. On 2026-08-10 the vault page was missing --slot-save-path and --moe-stream-l2 32, while README.md and install.ps1 carried them. Nobody had changed anything wrongly; the copies simply drifted, and a measurement taken against the older line is not comparable to one taken against the newer.
_how_this_is_checked: tools/check_operating_point.py reads the RAW text of README.md and install.ps1 and extracts the flags from it. It must never read a second copy of this file - a checker that compares a manifest against itself is green forever.
_source_of_truth: This file. README.md and install.ps1 are renderings of it for humans; the measurement scripts take their defaults from it.

model._note: Not part of the install: 84.6 GiB and somebody else's artefact. 327,614,463 B per expert across 43 layers, read from the tensor tables of all three shards and confirmed by the server's own line (18,121.38 MiB / 58 slots = 312.44 MiB). The embedded chat template fails golden vector 4, which is why the operating point carries --chat-template-file.
model._why_this_rung: Moved from UD-IQ3_XXS on 2026-08-12, #89. Measured against it on the ten-task gate, three graded runs per rung, own server per run: 30/30 correct against 30/30, and the single deviation (two-sum, iq2-r2, DOES NOT RUN) is the extractor dropping an import placed above the function, not the model -- the answer was complete and correct. Throughput on the same tasks: decode 18.63 -> 19.53 tok/s (+4.8 %), ms per miss 0.7097 -> 0.6470 (-8.8 %), VRAM after load 31,074 -> 27,994 MiB. Prefill on a 1,884-token prompt 118.26 -> 133.10 (+12.6 %). The mechanism is bytes per miss, not cache slots: the hit rate moved 0.11 points across a 13.38 % smaller slab.
model._what_is_not_measured_on_this_rung: The slot ladder (56/58/60/62/64) and the host-tier pairing were measured on UD-IQ3_XXS and have NOT been repeated here. 58 slots is carried over unchanged, which is safe rather than optimal: the smaller slab leaves about 4.6 GB of card free after load against IQ3's 2.0 GB, so a larger cache would fit -- but 0731 covers 95 % of selections in 9.0 % of experts and 58 slots is already 2.5x past that, so more slots buy nothing measurable. Also unmeasured on this rung: the vendor KLD gap (0.30789 -> 0.48487, top-1 81.93 % -> 76.60 %) against anything other than ten algorithmic tasks.

models._what: Every GGUF a measurement script may point at, by key. tools/model-paths.ps1 reads this; nothing else spells a model path out.
models._why: Measured 2026-08-10: 26 lines across 18 files carried a model path, and 22 of those 26 pointed at files that no longer exist. Not one script was broken by it -- they all take -Model as a parameter, so the dead path is a default nobody notices until a run silently measures the wrong thing, or a model switch has to find 18 files.

operating-point.role: the operating point 0.2.0 ships. Moved here from UD-IQ3_XXS on 2026-08-12 (#89). This key has been wrong once before: on 2026-08-11 it still named the preview GGUF while the file above said 0731, so every script calling Get-ModelPath operating-point without -Model measured the model the release had already replaced -- that is how the prefill series in runs/2026-08-10/before-0731/ ended up published under a 0731 heading. A rung change therefore moves THIS key, not only model.quant
operating-point._needs: --chat-template-file manifests/0731-chat-template.jinja -- the embedded template fails the model's own golden vector 4
operating-point._sampling_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE, AND NOT ABSENT. This model takes the sampling block above unchanged -- temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, min_p 0.01, and NO top_k. An empty override says that was decided; a missing key would say nobody looked. #112 leaves this model untouched deliberately: it is the one under measurement, and its 0731 series would not be comparable across a sampling change.
operating-point._reasoning_levels_note: What cli/crow.py offered for every model before #112, kept here unchanged for this one. This list records what may be SENT; reasoning_groups below records what is DISTINCT, and the two are not the same length.
operating-point._reasoning_groups_note: MEASURED 2026-08-21 (#117) through /apply-template against a running server on this exact GGUF, same four messages and one tool for every case. off (key absent), low and high all render sha256 fb2ba7d332bc at 1330 B; max renders b5a469609c08 at 1806 B, and the 476 B are the reasoning_effort_max block. So TWO of the three levels this table offers change nothing. The template agrees: manifests/0731-chat-template.jinja names reasoning_effort in exactly one condition, line 64, '{%- if thinking and reasoning_effort == max -%}', and sets the absent key to none at lines 12-13 -- there is no low branch and no high branch. enable_thinking was measured too and is irrelevant: max differs without it, and setting it moves no byte. NOTE that cli/crow_core.py's comment near line 2483 says this template reads an absent key as low; that is wrong, low does not occur in the file.

0731-iq3-xxs.role: alias of operating-point, for scripts that name the model generation. Downloaded and header-verified 2026-08-10. 378,208,256 B per expert. That is 288 MiB more per 64-slot cache than the preview, and it is what pushed 64 slots over the card: see server._moe_stream_cache_note

0731-iq2-xxs.role: alias of operating-point since 0.2.0, for scripts that name the quantisation. Downloaded and header-verified 2026-08-12: three shards, 5,257,664 + 49,890,588,800 + 40,964,890,464 B, 0 + 728 + 600 tensors, difference 0 on each. NOTE that this key names shard 1, which carries 0 tensors and 5 MB of metadata -- Get-ModelPath -MustExist is satisfied by it while the 90 GiB of weights beside it may be absent, which is exactly the state this file was in for six hours on 2026-08-12. The server's own expert cache line is the check that cannot be fooled: 18,121.38 MiB / 58 = 312.44 MiB per slot against 360.69 for iq3, i.e. 13.38 % smaller. Measured on it (#89): decode +4.8 %, ms per miss -8.8 %, hit rate -0.11 points, gate 30/30 -- two thirds of a byte reduction converts to stall on this drive, the rest is latency

preview-iq3-xxs.role: the model 0.0.6 shipped, kept for the before-side comparison in runs/2026-08-10/before-0731/. NOT the operating point since 0.1.0

iq3-xxs.role: alias of preview-iq3-xxs. Names a quantisation, not a generation -- 0731 ships the same quantisation, so this key is ambiguous by construction and kept only for scripts written before the switch

qwen35-q4-k-xl._sampling_note: ONLY WHAT DIFFERS. temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95 come from the sampling block below and are not repeated here -- repeating them would be a second literal for the same value, which tools/check_operating_point.py counts and refuses. min_p is the one that matters: the model card says 0.0, the GGUF is silent, llama.cpp's server default is 0.05 and Crow hard-wires 0.01. Four sources, and 0.05 is what a request that omits the field actually gets. top_k 20 is BELT-AND-BRACES rather than a repair: measured 2026-08-20 on a running server, /props already reports 20 because the GGUF carries general.sampling.top_k = 20 and llama.cpp applies it. #112's body claimed the server would run at 40; it does not. Stating it costs nothing and stops the value depending on GGUF metadata nobody re-reads.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._reasoning_levels_note: Measured 2026-08-20 (#108) against unsloth's embedded template, which is the one this model runs. ACCEPTED: low, medium, high, xhigh. REJECTED, they throw: max, none. And high, xhigh and the UNSET case render byte-identically -- sha256 a83d85ce715f -- so there are three distinct steps, not four. xhigh is left out because it is high under another name, and max is left out because it raises: of the three cli/crow.py offered before #112, one of them died on this model.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._reasoning_groups_note: MEASURED 2026-08-21 (#117), re-run of #108's finding with the group shape the window needs. Same four messages and one tool for every case: medium 1295 B sha256 3947591bf91b, low 1433 B 1a19dd82f362, off (key absent) and high both 1504 B 7aafe8ffbf9c. Different hashes from #108's a83d85ce715f because the message set differs; the GROUPING is what both runs agree on. The rendered instruction is the whole difference -- medium writes NO reasoning sentence at all and the system block starts at '# Tools', which is why medium is the cheapest step and not the middle one. The template's own error names the ladder: 'Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low'. off lands on xhigh because the absent key takes the default, so off is the DEAREST setting under a name that reads like the cheapest.

servers._what: One server command line per model key. The keys are the keys of models.entries above, so a line and the GGUF it starts are named by the same word.
servers._why: A second model brings a second command line, and until #111 the checker took the FIRST region of a file that matched and never looked at the rest -- so the second line would have been unchecked prose sitting next to a checked one, which is the exact shape the whole manifest exists to prevent. Now every key here must find its own matching region in README.md and install.ps1, and a failure names the key.
servers._how_the_keys_stay_apart: NOT by order, and not by the port alone. Each entry declares only the flags its line carries, and a region satisfies a key only if it carries ALL of them: the 0731 line has --moe-stream and --chat-template-file and no -ctk, the Qwen line has -ctk/-ctv q8_0 and neither of the other two. Neither region can satisfy the other's key. If a future pair of models ever declares the same flag set, they must differ in some flag or the checker cannot tell which line it found.

operating-point._moe_stream_cache_note: 58 and not 64, measured 2026-08-11 (#87, evidence on #86). A slot costs 360.69 MiB - the server prints the cache size at every step and the figure is constant to five digits. The ladder, with the number of runs behind each cell, VRAM read after load out of 32,607 MiB: 64 -> prefill 15.28 median of 8 with spread 8.69x, no 200-token decode series taken, 32,014 used / 593 free; 62 -> prefill 114.92 median of 5, decode 14.62 median of 4 with one request at 7.07, 31,683 / 924; 60 -> 113.53 median of 5, 17.43 median of 8, 30,954 / 1,653; 58 -> 112.69 median of 3, 17.32 median of 8, 30,548 / 2,059; 56 -> 110.30 median of 3, 17.09 median of 8, 29,842 / 2,765. THE ARITHMETIC IS THE EVIDENCE: 62 reads 31,683 and 60 reads 30,954, i.e. 729 MiB for two slots against the 721 the printed slot size predicts, so 64 must read about 32,404 - and it reads 32,014. Those 390 MiB are what the driver moved to host memory without printing anything, and the affected request then halves with identical graph executions, identical misses and the LOWEST load stall of its run. 58 against 60 is NOT a throughput difference (112.69 vs 113.53, 17.32 vs 17.43, while repeating one configuration eight times spans 1.09x) - what separates them is the margin. CAUTION ON READING THE LADDER AS ONE SERIES: 58 and 56 were taken in one session and 62 and 60 in another, and a VRAM reading always contains whatever else was on the card at that moment. THE VALUE IS THIS CARD'S, NOT A CONSTANT: derived from 32,607 MiB of VRAM and whatever the display holds beside it.
operating-point._chat_template_file_note: 0731 ships no Jinja template and its GGUF embeds one that fails golden vector 4 (the action turn). The verified template ships with the package as templates/0731-chat-template.jinja; the checker requires the FLAG in every copy of the command line and, like moe_stream_l2, not a specific path -- installs differ.

qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_mmproj: MEASURED 2026-08-27 (#142). The model is a vision model and ran blind from day one: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF ships mmproj-F16.gguf (927,607,488 B), and without the flag /props says modalities.vision false. Measured with it against the same 27,730-token prompt, 3 runs each, cold cache: prefill 2,864.36 -> 2,849.41 tok/s (-0.5 %, inside both spreads), VRAM after load 27,991 -> 29,115 MiB, so the projector holds 1,124 MiB. One image costs (w/32)*(h/32) tokens after llama.cpp's smart-resize plus 2 markers, hard-capped at 4,096 = 2.0 % of the window -- measured on six images, zero deviation from the formula. The value is a path relative to the model roots, like models.entries.path, because the projector sits beside its GGUF in both trees. A model whose line has no mmproj key is text-only BY DESIGN, not by omission; a declared projector missing on disk boots text-only with a sentence (start_server), never silently. F16 over BF16: same size to 0.4 %, and F16 is the variant this machine measured. Raw runs: crow-lab/runs/2026-08-27-vision/.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_spec_type: MEASURED 2026-08-21, and it is the largest single win this model has produced. The GGUF ships its own multi-token-prediction head -- nextn_predict_layers = 1, tensors blk.64.nextn.eh_proj / enorm / hnorm / shared_head_norm -- and the command line left it idle until this date. Same prompt, same file, cold server, reasoning high: decode 123.05 tok/s against 66.51 without the flag on the tool-heavy prompt, 133.18 against 64.50 on the warm follow-up. Client and server agree to the digit -- the eleven eval-time blocks sum to 53.564 s for 6,591 tokens, and the eleven prompt-eval lines to 20,490. THE MECHANISM IS NOT FREE MULTIPLICATION: drafting costs 37 % of the pass rate, 65 main-model passes per second down to 41, and pays it back through 2.98 accepted tokens per pass. Acceptance over the turn was 4,379 of 6,630 drafted, 66 %, and per round it ran from 52 % on the big file-reading turn to 100 % on a short one. Quality was graded on the same run and is unchanged: every line number, the flag order and both format lines correct. NOT the same finding as 0731's, where a SEPARATE draft model costs 6 % because the streamed operating point pays in bytes -- this head lives inside the model and needs no second file. UNMEASURED: --spec-draft-n-max, which defaults to 3; at full acceptance the same 41 passes would carry 165 tok/s, so there is headroom nobody has looked at.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._measured: 2026-08-20, #106 and #108. Loads in 7.9 s on the b10269 build (crow-lab/wt-25, 1c3c967) -- the UNPATCHED stock build loads it identically (25,594 against 25,561 MiB, 33 MiB of noise), so src/llama-mmap.cpp is out of the picture and the base jump this stage was planned around is not needed.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_q8_0_kv: MEASURED, not chosen. f16 KV left 332.8 MiB of headroom -- a third of the 924 MiB this file documents at server._moe_stream_cache_note as the point where losses start. With q8_0 the card holds 25,253-25,561 MiB with 6,627 free, and the KV is 6,647.00 MiB against 6,645.8 predicted. flash_attn is switched on by the server itself, because a quantised V demands it.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_not_moe_stream: This is a 16.4 GB dense model that fits on the card whole. --moe-stream routes EXPERT tensors through a slot cache and there are none; the flag would be a copied habit, and a flag in a line people copy is a recommendation.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_no_chat_template_file: Unlike 0731, this GGUF's embedded template is the one to use -- unsloth's. #108 measured it: reasoning_effort low/medium/high are accepted, max and none throw, and high, xhigh and the unset case render byte-identically (sha256 a83d85ce715f), so there are three real steps and not four.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_port_8082: 8081 is the client's default and 0731's port. The two models are alternatives, not a pair, but they were measured side by side and every raw run under runs/2026-08-20/ carries 8082 -- so a client pointed here needs --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1. Changing it would orphan those runs.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._not_measured: Decode at a full window: the 71.05 tok/s figure comes from a 16-token prompt at an EMPTY context and is not an operating value. Prefill is 3,163.9 / 3,236.4 / 3,020.5 tok/s at 4,028 / 16,006 / 32,012 tokens -- already not linear, so do not extrapolate to 200k. Crow never reaches 200k anyway: ROLLOVER_AT = 0.9 in cli/crow_core.py cuts at 180,000.

flash-next-q2-k-xl._env_history: CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE=1 stood here for three hours on 2026-08-28 night and was MEASURED WORSE: with the driver cache skipped, in-service deaths went from hourly to every few minutes -- every fresh kernel shape hits the driver JIT, and this machine's JIT is the organ that rolls CUDA 303 'shared object initialization failed'. The flag had cured only the BOOT class, and only because the on-disk cache held a corrupt entry (set aside as ComputeCache.korrupt-2026-08-28; the fresh cache boots fine without any flag). The open root cause is the driver install itself (616.56, first sustained load tonight; 610.88 ran for days) -- robins call.
flash-next-q2-k-xl._why_binary: arch qwen4exp exists only in llama.cpp PR #27742; the shipped engine cannot load it. Build 439 (250b614) is the named one BY MEASUREMENT: the newer PR head eaf9376 (build 453) is 3-6 % faster when it boots and fails the warmup 11 of 19 times -- CUDA 'shared object initialization failed', uniform signature, A/B under identical driver 616.56 on 2026-08-28 (439: 13/13). A LAB ARTIFACT, not shipped -- this entry exists so the operating point can be tested from the repo; shipping it is the open product decision on #140, license gate included.
flash-next-q2-k-xl._why_port_8083: 8081 is 0731's port, 8082 the 27B's. Every raw run of the #140 series (crow-lab/runs/2026-08-28-flash-next/, 60+ rows) carries 8083; changing it would orphan them.
flash-next-q2-k-xl._why_load_mode_none: mmap at the RAM ceiling reads the NVMe into every token: all eight grid rows ran at 63.03-63.19 of 63.38 GiB RAM with tg_3s dips 24 -> 3.8 tok/s, identical configs spread 19-31 tok/s on page-cache luck, and the build itself warns at boot. With none, CPU experts sit in anonymous memory (~47 GiB, 16 free) and two runs of the same line differ by 0.16 % prefill / 0.1 % decode. The price moves into the boot: ~68 s instead of ~13 s, paid once.
flash-next-q2-k-xl._why_ncmoe_40: The stable optimum of the #140 sweep. Fewer CPU layers ride the VRAM edge: at >= ~31.9 GiB used the prefill collapses 941 -> 135-250 and nc32/200k/lm-none dies in the first turn (2 of 2). nc24 boots into WDDM spill at 2.70-3.40 tok/s decode. The decode curve nc36-nc40 is flat; the ceiling is the 40 GPU<->CPU transitions per token, not DDR5 bandwidth (naive ceiling ~78 tok/s, measured ~36 % of it).
flash-next-q2-k-xl._measured: 2026-08-28, driver 616.56, build 439, 10-boot series with a 31,979-token cold turn each: 10/10 boots, prefill 964.8 tok/s mean (949.99-981.03), decode 28.61 mean (27.01-29.37), VRAM 28.4 GiB after the turn (4.2 free), RAM ~46.6 GiB, load-to-health 62.3-84.8 s. Against the 27B operating point (123.05 / 2,262.96): decode x0.23, prefill x0.43. Raw rows: crow-lab/runs/2026-08-28-flash-next/results.csv; the three measurement comments sit on #140.
flash-next-q2-k-xl._not_measured: This exact Crow shape (-np 1 AND --jinja AND q8 KV in one line) pending the boot check below; the embedded chat template against golden vectors and tool turns; reasoning levels via /apply-template; slot save with the hybrid's recurrent state -- slot_save_path is OMITTED on purpose until someone measures that a linear-attention state survives a save/restore; speculation: MTP head absent, ngram net -2 %, a 27B drafter halves decode at 0.775 acceptance (no small Qwen3.8 GGUF exists to draft with).

sampling._what: What the client and every probe send when nobody says otherwise.
sampling._why: 1.0 / 0.95 is what DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 specifies. THE SOURCES DISAGREE and the disagreement belongs here rather than in anyone's memory: the model card (manifests/0731-encoding/model-card.md) runs its agentic benchmarks at temperature 1.0 with top_p 0.95; the model's own generation_config.json says temperature 1.0 with top_p 1.0. Crow is an agent, so the agentic figure wins for top_p. 0.6 was the PREVIEW family's value and shipped in every release up to 0.0.6.
sampling._why_not_zero: 0.0 is greedy decoding, and greedy is where reasoning models loop: measured 2026-08-07 on a three.js task, the model repeated 'Actually, let me...' inside its reasoning block and never reached the answer. That holds for 0731 as much as for the preview.
sampling._min_p_note: unsloth's docs recommend 0.01 for this model; DeepSeek's own card is silent on it. Sent explicitly because llama.cpp's server default is 0.05 -- not sending it means inheriting a THIRD value nobody chose, the same omission top_p was until #83. robin approved shipping it 2026-08-10.
sampling._measurement_note: temperature 0 in a probe is a MEASUREMENT decision, not a model default: it buys byte-reproducible output. Those literals stay where they are. And any A/B across the model switch must pin --temperature explicitly on BOTH sides -- the default changed with 0731, and a comparison that inherits it measures the sampling change and the model change in one number.

moe_stream_l2._note: Windows reports 63.4 on a 64 GB machine, so a threshold at the nominal size would exclude exactly the configuration this was measured on. install.ps1 prints the flag with a machine-dependent value, so the checker accepts any integer there and only requires the flag itself.

decode_baseline._note: The promise 0.1 had to keep -- the PREVIEW model on 0.0.6. Kept for comparison; the measured 0.1 figures are in decode_measured_0731.

decode_measured_0731.method: median of three pairs, same driver and graded tasks as the baseline
decode_measured_0731._note: The promise held: +29.9 % over the baseline median, and even the worst tier arm (16.17) beats the old median. Within-arm spread 1.19x, wider than the baseline's 1.09x -- the band is indicative, the direction clears the noise. TAKEN AT 64 SLOTS, i.e. at the configuration #87 replaces: it is a single sitting on a setup now known to scatter, so it is the bar the new value had to clear rather than a figure that still describes the product.

decode_measured_0731_62s.method: median of three paired arms, one warm-up plus two graded tasks each, fresh server per arm, temperature unpinned - the same arrangement as the 19.13 above
decode_measured_0731_62s._note: The criterion was fixed before the run: the median had to reach the 19.13 above. Stall per miss is the more robust of the two figures (run-l2-pairs.ps1 says why) and comes out at 0.707-0.720 against 0.717-0.741 at 64 slots - a smaller cache produces more misses and the individual miss still does not cost more. No fresh 64-slot arm was taken alongside; the comparison is against the recorded bar.

prefill_measured_0731.condition: COLD expert cache, fresh server, machine idle, stderr to a file
prefill_measured_0731._note: The 64-slot figures are the median and spread of eight runs of one configuration - the value is not reproducible there, which is the defect #87 fixes. Warm prefill is not this number; nothing here describes a warm cache. The prompt is a repeated word list from the harness, which routes to fewer distinct experts than real text, so it is the upper end of a cold start rather than the middle.

vram_measured_0731._note: Free is 32,607 minus the reading, and it has to cover everything the display does. Read identically in all three runs of the series. At 62 slots the margin is 924 MiB and single requests halved at random; at 64 the allocation no longer fits at all and 390 MiB are missing from the reading.

decode_measured_0731_58s._note: Eight consecutive requests on one server at four prompt sizes, temperature 0. The point of the series is the SPREAD: at 62 slots the same probe produced 7.07 among 15s, at 58 the widest gap is 1.09x. This is a probe, not the graded gate - for the gate at 58 slots see gate_measured_0731_58s below.

gate_measured_0731_58s.method: median of three paired arms at --moe-stream-cache 58s, one warm-up plus two graded tasks each, fresh server per arm, temperature unpinned - the same arrangement as the 19.81 at 62 slots and the 19.13 at 64
gate_measured_0731_58s.graded_correct: 6 of 6 with the tier, 6 of 6 without
gate_measured_0731_58s.median_arm: r3-l2: 3 answers, 837 tokens, 46,434.23 ms; base r3-base: 3 answers, 1,139 tokens, 103,196.15 ms
gate_measured_0731_58s._note: The gate at the SHIPPED operating point, run 2026-08-11 after 0.1.1 went out.
